parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of the file is ordinary application orchestration: it loads the order through the domain repository port, delegates the state change to the domain (order.transitionTo), and saves the order. The problem is that execute() takes untyped `any` inputs and unwraps raw HTTP request shapes itself. It checks `Array.isArray(orderId) ? orderId[0] : orderId`, and does the same for newState with `newState[0]?.toString()`, plus a `typeof newState === 'string'` check. This is how Express-style route and query parameters (string | string[] | ParsedQs) are handled. Parsing and normalizing transport input is the job of the infrastructure/presentation adapter (OrderController, which the graph shows calling this use case). It is not an application-layer job. The use case should accept typed inputs such as (orderId: string, newState: OrderStateType). The unchecked cast `stateStr as OrderStateType` also means input validation is done ad hoc here instead of at the boundary.
